blocks.text: Add vertex work and stored-edge work

items: Discovering and processing each vertex once contributes O(V).
The sum of adjacency-list lengths is E for a directed graph and 2E for an undirected graph, both O(E).
Therefore total traversal time is O(V) + O(E) = O(V + E).
Visited stores at most V marks and the queue or stack at most O(V) vertices, so auxiliary space is O(V).

blocks.text: Under adjacency lists, charge each vertex once and each stored edge entry once.
blocks.title: Accounting rule

feedback.reason: Each vertex is discovered once and adjacency-list scans total the stored edge entries; visited plus frontier can hold O(V) state.

prompt: A complete BFS or iterative DFS traverses every vertex and edge entry of a graph stored as adjacency lists. Each vertex is discovered once. Derive worst-case traversal time and auxiliary space, excluding the input representation and output.

blocks.text: A matrix charges every possible neighbor pair

items: All V vertices are reached.
Each reached vertex scans a row of V matrix cells, including absent edges.
The product V · V gives O(V²) traversal time.
Visited plus frontier still contains only vertex state, so auxiliary space is O(V); the excluded input matrix is O(V²).

blocks.text: For E = Θ(V²), matrix time O(V²) matches O(V + E); on sparse graphs it pays for absent pairs.
blocks.title: Dense boundary

feedback.reason: V reached vertices each trigger a scan of V potential neighbors, while visited and frontier remain linear in V.

prompt: A traversal of a graph with V vertices uses an adjacency matrix and, for every reached vertex, scans its entire matrix row. All vertices are reached. Derive worst-case time and auxiliary space, excluding the matrix itself and output.

blocks.text: Linear work can still create linear call depth

items: Adjacency-list accounting gives O(V + E) time; for this path E = V − 1, so that bound is linear.
DFS enters vertex 1 from 0, vertex 2 from 1, and continues until the final vertex before unwinding.
The active recursive chain reaches V frames, and visited also uses O(V), so auxiliary space is O(V).

blocks.text: An explicit stack avoids a shallow call-stack limit but does not improve the O(V) worst-case auxiliary bound.
blocks.title: Implementation risk

feedback.reason: The path still scans each vertex and edge once, while recursive depth reaches V and visited also uses O(V).

prompt: Recursive DFS traverses an adjacency-list graph whose reachable component is a simple path of V vertices. Derive worst-case time and auxiliary space, counting the recursion stack and visited state but excluding input and output.

blocks.text: A wide layer fills the queue

items: The star has V vertices and E = V − 1 edges, scanned in O(V + E) time.
Expanding the center discovers and enqueues all V − 1 leaves before any leaf is removed.
Queue width is therefore V − 1 = O(V), and visited is also O(V).

blocks.text: BFS auxiliary space follows maximum frontier width, which can be linear even in a sparse graph.
blocks.title: Breadth-space boundary

feedback.reason: All vertices and edge entries are scanned once, and one BFS layer can place nearly all vertices in the queue together.

prompt: BFS traverses an adjacency-list graph consisting of a source connected to V−1 leaves. Derive worst-case time and auxiliary space, excluding input and output.

blocks.text: Component traversals partition the work

items: The outer scan examines V vertices once, contributing O(V).
Visited ensures each vertex is expanded by exactly one component traversal.
Across all components, adjacency-list scans still total O(E), not E per component.
Thus time is O(V + E), while visited and the largest active frontier use O(V) auxiliary space.

blocks.text: Multiple traversal starts do not multiply work when their visited regions are disjoint.
blocks.title: Amortized rule

feedback.reason: The outer loop adds O(V), but visited state ensures the inner traversals partition rather than repeat graph work.

prompt: Connected components are counted by scanning all V vertices and starting an adjacency-list traversal whenever a vertex is unseen. Across all components, derive worst-case time and auxiliary space, excluding input and output.

blocks.text: Late marking changes the unit from vertices to edge exposures

items: With mark-on-enqueue, each vertex creates at most one queue entry, so frontier storage is O(V).
With mark-on-dequeue, several processed predecessors can enqueue the same still-unmarked target.
In a guarded simple graph, each examined edge can generate a copy, yielding O(E) queue operations and potentially O(E) pending entries.
Skipping stale copies before neighbor scans can retain O(V + E) time; expanding them can increase work further.

blocks.text: Equal final reachability does not imply equal frontier-space or queue-operation bounds.
blocks.title: Operational warning

messages.text: Final reachability does not capture duplicate enqueue operations or the larger frontier they can create.
Multiple predecessors can still observe an unmarked vertex before dequeue; representation does not supply queued state.
The exact penalty depends on graph structure and duplicate handling; O(V²) is not universal.

feedback.reason: Each examined edge can publish another copy before the target's first dequeue, so queue-entry count is no longer bounded by vertices.

options.text: Time and space are always identical to discovery-time marking because both eventually visit the same vertices.
The time is necessarily O(V²) for every graph.
The result can remain correct, but up to O(E) queue entries may be generated, weakening the usual O(V) frontier bound.
Converting to an adjacency matrix restores one enqueue per vertex without changing visited timing.

prompt: BFS marks a vertex visited only when dequeued and has no separate queued-state check. Duplicate copies are skipped when popped after the first processed copy. Which resource warning is justified for a simple adjacency-list graph?

blocks.text: Substitute grid dimensions into graph accounting

items: The grid has at most V = R · C reachable cell states.
Four candidate checks per state give at most 4RC = O(RC) neighbor work.
Therefore traversal time is O(RC).
The separate visited grid stores RC flags and the frontier can hold O(RC) cells, so auxiliary space is O(RC).

blocks.text: In-place marking can remove the separate visited allocation only when consuming the input is contract-safe.
blocks.title: Mutation boundary

feedback.reason: There are RC states, each checks only a constant number of moves, and visited/frontier can each scale with the state count.

prompt: A traversal visits every reachable cell of an R × C grid, generates at most four neighbors per cell, and uses a separate visited grid plus a BFS queue or DFS stack. Derive worst-case time and auxiliary space, excluding the input grid and output.

blocks.text: Kahn charges every vertex and edge once

items: Initialize V indegree counters in O(V).
Scan E edges to populate indegrees in O(E).
Each vertex enters the ready queue at most once, adding O(V).
Each outgoing edge causes exactly one decrement, adding O(E).

blocks.text: The sum is O(V + E). Indegrees plus the ready queue use O(V) auxiliary space; the input adjacency is excluded. A matrix would change neighbor scanning toward O(V²), not the readiness invariant.
Time O(V + E), auxiliary space O(V).
blocks.title: Kahn bound

feedback.reason: Indegree construction and updates touch every vertex and edge once; indegrees plus the ready queue are linear in vertices.

prompt: Kahn's topological algorithm runs on a sparse directed graph stored as outgoing adjacency lists. It builds an indegree array, processes each vertex once, and decrements once per edge. Derive worst-case time and auxiliary space, excluding input adjacency and output order.

blocks.text: Sources add initialization, not repeated traversals

items: Enumerating and seeding k distinct sources costs O(k).
The shared queue discovers each reachable vertex once and scans each reached adjacency entry once, bounded by O(V + E).
Total time is O(k + V + E), which simplifies to O(V + E) because distinct sources satisfy k ≤ V.
Visited, distances and the shared queue each require at most O(V) space.

blocks.text: O(k(V + E)) describes k separate BFS runs, not one multi-source frontier.
blocks.title: Do not multiply by k

blocks.text: One shared traversal adds O(k) seeding and retains O(V) auxiliary space.
blocks.title: Multi-source bound

feedback.reason: Seeding costs O(k), after which the shared traversal processes each discovered vertex and edge entry once rather than once per source.

prompt: A multi-source BFS on an adjacency-list graph seeds k distinct sources once, then discovers each reachable vertex at most once. Derive worst-case time and auxiliary space in terms of the whole graph, excluding input and output.
